title: Normalized finite dualizing complexes when the reduction is regular
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$. Let $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism of a nonempty separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that its reduction $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ (the closed subscheme obtained by quotienting the structure sheaf by its nilradical) is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and that $|X|$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Put $d=\dim|X|$, using topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For $n\geq1$ put $\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. On the small etale sites use bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and the finite-coefficient exceptional adjoint $a_n^!$ of $Ra_!$ appearing in [lem-per-adic-exceptional-projection]. There are isomorphisms
$$a_n^!(\Lambda_n)_k\cong \Lambda_{n,X}(d)[2d],$$
where $\Lambda_{n,X}(0)$ is the coefficient sheaf and, for $d>0$, $\Lambda_{n,X}(d)=\mu_{\ell^n,X}^{\otimes_{\Lambda_{n,X}}d}$. Here $\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ is the etale sheaf of units $u$ with $u^{\ell^n}=1$, with its $\Lambda_n$-module structure given by exponentiation. These twists are locally free of rank one. The isomorphisms may be chosen compatibly with derived coefficient reduction $\Lambda_{n+1}\to\Lambda_n$: under them the reduction tower of $a_n^!(\Lambda_n)_k[-2d]$ is the ordinary tower of rank-one sheaves $\Lambda_{n,X}(d)$, whose transition on roots of unity is $u\mapsto u^\ell$. The normalization is the relative dimension function $x\mapsto\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)$, with coefficient unit at $\operatorname{Spec}k$. No perfectness or separable-generation hypothesis on $k$ or $X/k$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.4.1, Proposition 4.1.2 and Remark 4.1.3, Theorem 5.1.1, and proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1 (printed p.294); regular normalized potential complex and finite-type exceptional normalization. Coherent finite reduction as in Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.7.20.

external.place: Proof of Lemma 6.7.20: normalized potential dualizing complexes at all Z/ell^n stages and compatible derived reductions.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $T=X_{\mathrm{red}}$, $i:T\hookrightarrow X$ and $b=a i$. Finite-type affine coordinate rings over $k$ are excellent: apply excellence of fields and stability under finite-type algebras (localizations included). Excellence includes Noetherianity, and finite type provides a finite affine cover. This applies to $X$ and to the quotient-coordinate rings of $T$. Thus both are Noetherian excellent and ell is invertible on them. Nagata compactification applies to $a$ and $b$, since the base $s$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and both structure maps are separated of finite type. The reduction inclusion is proper because it is a closed immersion. Its underlying space is $|X|$, so $T$ is nonempty and irreducible, in particular connected. The finite-type dimension bound makes $d$ a finite nonnegative integer. Since the base field is locally Noetherian, the locally-finite-type to locally-finitely-presented theorem applies to a and b; finite type gives quasi-compactness and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness, so both maps are finitely presented, as required for the coefficient comparison.

source.place: XVII, hypotheses for Proposition 4.1.2; Stacks excellence and compactification preparation

proof.text: For each $n$, apply the finite etale twist theorem with $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ and exponent $\ell^n$. It gives the etale rank-one line $\Lambda_{n,X}(d)$ and its pullback identification $i^{-1}\Lambda_{n,X}(d)\cong\Lambda_{n,T}(d)$. It also identifies the exponent-change comparison with the power map $u\mapsto u^\ell$. All coefficient and twist sheaves here are on the small etale sites. This supplies the claimed local freeness without assuming that $k$ contains roots of unity.

Write $c(t)=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Since $T$ is irreducible and locally of finite type over $k$, its dimension at every point is $d$. The finite-type dimension formula therefore gives $d=c(t)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(t)$. Hence the desired normalization on $T$ is $\delta_T(t)=d-c(t)$. At the generic point $c=0$, so this normalization has value $d$. No smoothness or separability has been used.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1, regular connected case; finite-type dimension formula

proof.text: The regular-unit theorem equips $\Lambda_{n,s}$ with potential pinnings for the zero dimension function. Apply finite-type extraordinary pullback to $a$ and to $b$. It equips $a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$ with the relative function $x\mapsto\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)$ and equips $b_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$ with the same function on $T$. The comparison $i_n^!a_n^!\cong b_n^!$ preserves these pinnings. Since $T$ is regular, the regular-unit theorem with $m=d$ equips $\Lambda_{n,T}(d)[2d]$ with potential pinnings for $d-c(t)$, which is exactly the function calculated in step 3.

Apply uniqueness with fixed pinnings on $(T,\delta_T)$ to the two objects from step 4. This gives a pinning-preserving isomorphism $\theta_{n,T}:b_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{n,T}(d)[2d]$. The same uniqueness theorem puts the normalized potential objects in $D^b_c$ with finite Tor amplitude, so this is also an isomorphism in the constructible category specified in the item. It is the fixed pinnings, rather than an arbitrary choice of a dualizing object, that select the isomorphism.

source.place: XVII, Theorem 5.1.1 and proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1

proof.text: The map $i$ is a universal homeomorphism: on every affine base change it is the spectrum of a quotient by an ideal generated by nilpotent elements, and such a quotient has exactly the same prime ideals. Topological invariance makes $i^{-1}$ and $i_*$ inverse exact equivalences of etale topoi. Their module versions are also exact inverse equivalences, since the coefficient sheaves are constant, and applying them termwise gives inverse derived equivalences. For proper $i$, its compactification with identity open immersion computes $Ri_!=Ri_*$; the compactification comparisons identify this with the compact-support functor in the adjunction. The right adjoint of the equivalence $Ri_*$ is its inverse $i^{-1}$, so uniqueness of right adjoints gives $i_n^!\cong i^{-1}$. Together with step 4, this identifies $i^{-1}(a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s})$ with $b_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$. Pullback of the twist was identified in step 2. Full faithfulness now lifts $\theta_{n,T}$ uniquely to an isomorphism $\theta_{n,X}:a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{n,X}(d)[2d]$. Finally, this is the constructible adjoint of the statement. The object $\Lambda_{n,X}(d)[2d]$ lies in $D^b_c$, and by [lem-per-adic-exceptional-projection] $Ra_!$ restricts to the full subcategories $D^b_c\subset D^+$ with a right adjoint $a_n^!$ there. For $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda_n)$ the bounded-below adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(K,a^!_{+}\Lambda_{n,s})=\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!K,\Lambda_{n,s})$, where $a^!_{+}$ is the bounded-below adjoint of the potential nodes. So the bounded-constructible object $a^!_{+}\Lambda_{n,s}$ represents the functor defining $a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$. By Yoneda the two agree, with the same counit, and the same holds for $b$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 6.2.2.1: reduction to the reduced case; etale topological invariance

proof.text: Apply the normalized coefficient-tower theorem to the potential objects of step 4. Its extraordinary-pullback clause identifies the actual derived coefficient reductions of $a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$ and $b_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$ with their normalized potential comparisons. The regular pinnings on $\Lambda_{n,T}(d)[2d]$ reduce to those for $n$. Consequently both routes around the square comparing $\theta_{n+1,T}\otimes^L\Lambda_n$ and $\theta_{n,T}$ preserve the same pinnings; uniqueness makes the square commute. To identify the target transition explicitly, locally choose a generator $\zeta$ of $\mu_{\ell^{n+1}}$; then $\zeta^\ell$ generates $\mu_{\ell^n}$. On these generators the power map is exactly the scalar quotient $\Lambda_{n+1}\to\Lambda_n$. The tensor power of this calculation gives reduction of the $d$th twist, with no higher Tor since it is locally free. Shifting by $-2d$ therefore gives precisely the ordinary rank-one tower in the statement. The base object at $s$ is the coefficient unit, so the normalization is the relative transcendence-degree function, including for imperfect $k$.

source.place: Bhatt–Scholze, Lemmas 6.7.18 and 6.7.20; ILO XVII, Theorem 5.1.1

proof.text: The lift in step 6 is also compatible with reduction. Let $\iota_n:i^{-1}a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}\cong i_n^!a_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}\cong b_n^!\Lambda_{n,s}$ be the step-6 identification. It preserves pinnings by the transitivity clause of finite-type extraordinary pullback (step 4, applied to $i$ and $a$). Compare two maps $(b^!_{n+1}\Lambda_{n+1,s})\otimes^L\Lambda_n\to b^!_n\Lambda_{n,s}$. The first is the coefficient-tower comparison $\rho^b_n$ for $b$. The second is $\iota_n\circ i^{-1}\rho^a_n\circ(\iota_{n+1}^{-1}\otimes^L\Lambda_n)$, using exactness of $i^{-1}$ and its commutation with constant-coefficient $\otimes^L$. Both preserve the pinnings. For the second, $\rho^a_n$ does by the tower theorem, and $i^{-1}=i^!$ carries pinning-preserving maps to pinning-preserving maps, since the pinnings of $i^!$ are natural. Uniqueness on $T$ makes the two maps equal. Hence $i^{-1}$ carries the coefficient square on $X$, formed by $\theta_{n+1,X}\otimes^L\Lambda_n$, $\theta_{n,X}$, $\rho^a_n$ and the twist reduction, to the commuting square on $T$ of step 7. Faithfulness of the equivalence $i^{-1}$ makes the square on $X$ commute. This gives the asserted compatibility of the isomorphisms on $X$ with derived coefficient reduction.
